prerequisites: Knowledge of the C/C++ programming language
Knowledge in the area of digital circuit design with VHDL

learning_outcomes.text: After completing the module, students will have in-depth knowledge in the field of hardware and software design for electronic systems. They can apply this knowledge to independently specify and realize systems.
Students are able to integrate independently developed subsystems into more complex systems.

After completing the module, students will have in-depth knowledge in the field of hardware/software design and are able to define different realization variants for a given task and evaluate them with regard to criteria such as effort and efficiency.
Students understand relevant aspects for the realization of electronic systems.
Students are able to define subsystems and realize them as hardware and software components.
Students are able to independently realize electronic systems using current design tools.
Students are able to analyze a given task. From the results of the analysis, they develop solution approaches and alternative realization variants.
Students can evaluate the variants and decide which variant is suitable for realization.
Students are able to carry out application-oriented projects and contribute to solving complex tasks in a team.
Students are able to investigate a problem and evaluate solution approaches.
They are able to construct new systems based on known basic structures and to examine and evaluate their properties.
Students can present the results of the analysis in a structured manner orally or in writing.
Students can realize simple systems and adequately represent the chosen approach to a specialist audience.

syllabus_topics: Tools for developing IP blocks and for system integration
Memory connection and communication of system components
Integration of hardware and software components
assessment_rules: The graded examination is either a project report (approx. 15-20 pages) with a 15-minute project explanation or an oral examination. The form of examination is chosen by the lecturer. The ungraded examination involves approximately 6 experimental sessions, each lasting 90 minutes.
